messages:
Mia Chen: Follow-up from the RFC spike — proposal for a 'connector-as-outbound-session' model for Private customers.
Mia Chen: Problem we kept hitting: customers with restrictive network egress (only outbound allowed) + orgs that refuse peering but need low-latency control plane.
Mia Chen: New idea = customers run a lightweight connector that establishes short-lived mTLS sessions to our regional relay pool. Connector only initiates outbound TCP to a small set of IPs/ports.
Mia Chen: Key properties:
- sessions are ephemeral (30–90s) to limit lateral movement risk
- mutual TLS using customer-scoped certs, rotated via our control plane
- multiplexing of control plane and dataplane signals over same connection
- per-tenant routing tags so relay can NAT/route to the right backend pool
Samir Patel: Nice. How does this differ from the sidecar relay we've discussed before?
Mia Chen: Good question — this is intentionally asymmetric: connector is outbound-only and dumb (no need to accept inbound). Relay does heavy lifting (routing, auth, metrics). Sidecar model assumed inbound reachability or peering.
Rafi Gomez: Biggest win I see is customers behind strict firewalls can still get the private control plane without peering. Also reduced SRE burden on cross-account peering configs.
Cheng Li: Concerns:
- latency/jitter when relay sits in a different AZ/region
- TLS session churn overhead at scale
- billing: egress costs on customer side vs our inter-region bandwidth
Anna V: For latency we can use regional relay pools and prefer same-region IPs. But we need health-checking + fast reconnect on failover.
Mia Chen: Right — plan is region-local relays, and connector will prefer same-region endpoint list. Relay pool will advertise region via DNS + static IPs for firewall allowlists.
Samir Patel: Certificate model?
Mia Chen: We issue short-lived client certs per-connector instance signed by our CA. The connector authenticates to control plane to fetch a client cert via a one-time bootstrap token (customer-supplied). After that all traffic uses mTLS.
Rafi Gomez: How do we handle cert rotation if the connector is air-gapped or long-lived? The connector must be able to request renewal outbound — so that fits.
Cheng Li: What about observability and tracing — we need per-request provenance so customers can map requests to their pods/instances.
Mia Chen: We'll include a signed identity header (X-Redwood-Conn-ID) inside the TLS session metadata and surface mapping in Console logs. Relay will attach a route-id to spans.
Anna V: Security: ephemeral sessions are good. But we should limit what connectors can request or do — RBAC on the cert (scoped to model endpoints, not arbitrary control plane ops).
Mia Chen: Agreed. Policy model: certs are scoped to tenant ID + allowed route prefixes. We'll enforce via the relay and control plane gate.
infra-bot: Note: spike showed ~11% CPU overhead on small connectors under 1k rps, and 2x more connections vs peering baseline.
Samir Patel: Are we comfortable with the connector resource footprint? Some customers will run it on tiny instances.
Mia Chen: We'll optimize binaries and offer a 'shared connector' mode where a single host-level daemon can multiplex multiple local workloads.
Rafi Gomez: Rollout plan idea:
1) Beta with 3 pilot customers (low-traffic, strict firewall needs)
2) Add region-local IP lists + docs for firewall allowlist
3) Add telemetry + RBAC hardening
4) Broader GA and migration tooling from peering to connectors (opt-in)
Cheng Li: Migration concerns: DNS TTLs, session draining, sticky NAT mappings. Need to design graceful cutover to avoid in-flight token loss.
Mia Chen: We'll provide a staged migration mode: run peering + connector concurrently, start routing a percentage of traffic over connector, monitor metrics, then flip.
Anna V: One more operational note: support must be able to request a live session dump. Relay should expose a safe snapshot API (no private keys) for troubleshooting.
Mia Chen: Action items:
- Cheng: spec the mTLS certificate lifecycle and cert claims (deadline: next Tue)
- Rafi: perf testing template (load shape, connection churn) and infra cost estimate (deadline: Friday)
- Samir: docs draft for pilot customers with firewall allowlist and bootstrap UX (PR by end of week)
- Anna: permissions model sketch for cert-scoped RBAC (coauthor with Cheng)
Mia Chen: If no objections, I'll merge this as the post-RFC direction and start scheduling pilots.
Samir Patel: I like it. :thumbsup:
Rafi Gomez: Sounds good to me.
Cheng Li: Minor nit — define reconnect backoff jitter to avoid thundering herd during region outage.
Mia Chen: Good call, will add exponential backoff + jitter.
Anna V: +1
infra-bot: Reminder: submit perf results to #eng-runtime when ready (automated checklist updated).
